# Market Data Package — CPI-U, monthly (inflation companion)

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Package | `cpi-u-monthly` |
| Package version | `1.0.0` |
| BLS series | **CUUR0000SA0** — CPI-U, U.S. city average, all items, **not seasonally adjusted** |
| Retrieved via | FRED `CPIAUCNS` (Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis republication of the BLS series) |
| Retrieved | 2026-09-10 |
| Coverage | 1913-01 through 2026-07 — **1362 monthly index observations** |
| Derived monthly rates | 1361 |
| Conforms to | `MARKET_DATA_ENGINE_REFERENCE_2026.md` §2 (contract), §5.1 (CPI-U), §10.2 (calendar alignment) |
| Companion package | `MARKET_DATA_FF_MONTHLY_PACKAGE_2026.md` (monthly market total return) |
| Status | **Candidate.** Not wired into the engine. See §6. |

## 1. What this package is, and what it is not

**It is** the monthly CPI-U index level and the monthly inflation rates derived from it, for historical purchasing-power escalation. It is the inflation companion the market-return package requires before monthly stepping is possible.

**It is not the Social Security COLA basis.** `MARKET §5.2` is explicit: SSA bases COLA on **CPI-W** (`CWUR0000SA0`), using a third-quarter average comparison and rounding to the nearest 0.1%. Do not drive COLA from this series. A separate CPI-W package, or the official SSA COLA history, is required for that — **not included here.**

**It is not seasonally adjusted, deliberately.** `MARKET §5.1` records BLS guidance that unadjusted data is recommended for escalation, and that unadjusted CPI is final when issued except for rare corrections, whereas seasonally adjusted CPI can be revised for up to five years. For historical replay, final-when-issued is the property that matters.

**It is not an individualized inflation measure.** Per BLS, CPI-U covers more than 90% of the U.S. population, excludes investment items, and is a conditional rather than complete cost-of-living measure. `MARKET §5.1` requires these limitations appear in user-facing explanations.

## 3. Series metadata (`MARKET §2`)

| Field | `cpi_index` | `cpi_monthly_rate` |
|---|---|---|
| Frequency | Monthly | Monthly |
| Timing | Month reference period (whole month) | Month over prior month |
| Seasonal adjustment | None | None |
| Revision policy | Final when issued, rare corrections | Inherits |
| Nominal or real | Index level | Rate |

## 4. Transform specification

Monthly rate, for a monthly-stepped engine:

~~~text
cpi_monthly_rate[m] = CPI[m] / CPI[m-1] - 1
~~~

Annual, per `MARKET §5.1` — **two valid conventions that answer different questions. The package must name which one an engine uses.**

~~~text
inflation_dec_to_dec[y]      = CPI[December y] / CPI[December y-1] - 1
inflation_annual_average[y]  = average(CPI[months in y]) / average(CPI[months in y-1]) - 1
~~~

`MARKET §5.1`: *"Do not mix December-to-December inflation with annual-average income growth without an explicit timing bridge."*

## 5. Which convention the current engine uses

The engine's `HIST_INFLATION` (98 annual values, 1928–2025) was compared against both conventions computed from this package.

| Convention | Overlap years | Mean difference | Median absolute difference | Max absolute difference | Years within 10 bp |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| December-to-December | 98 | -0.001 pp | **0.002 pp** | 0.063 pp | 98 of 98 |
| Annual average | 97 | -0.016 pp | **0.638 pp** | 9.654 pp | 13 of 97 |

**Conclusion: `HIST_INFLATION` is a December-to-December series.** It matches that convention to a median of 0.002 pp, with 98 of 98 years agreeing within 10 basis points. Any monthly package adopted must preserve this convention at the annual boundary, or the change must be audited as a financial model change in its own right.

## 6. Coverage and alignment with the market-return package

| | This package | `ff-market-monthly` |
|---|---|---|
| Starts | 1913-01 | 1926-07 |
| Ends | 2026-07 | 2026-07 |
| Timing | Whole-month reference period | Month-end |

**Common coverage is 1926-07 through 2026-07** — the market series is the binding constraint, and this package extends 13 years further back than any use will need.

**Timing mismatch, per `MARKET §10.2`:** CPI is a whole-month reference period; the market return is a month-end observation. These are not the same timing convention. The mismatch is small at monthly resolution but must be *labelled* rather than silently joined, exactly as §10.2 requires. Record the convention pair in the engine package metadata.

## 7. Validation invariants

1. **Row count.** Exactly 1362 index observations, contiguous monthly, 1913-01 to 2026-07, no gaps.
2. **Month continuity.** Each consecutive pair is exactly one calendar month apart.
3. **Index positivity.** Every `cpi_index` > 0.
4. **Rate bounds.** Every `cpi_monthly_rate` lies within (-0.10, 0.10). The observed extremes are -3.16% (1921-02) and 5.88% (1946-07); a value outside the bound means a parse or units error.
5. **Compounding identity.** For each complete year, the product of that year's twelve monthly rates minus 1 equals `inflation_dec_to_dec` for that year to within 1e-12 — because both are ratios of the same December endpoints.
6. **Convention pinning.** The ingesting build records which of the two §4 annual conventions it uses. An unnamed convention is a defect, not a default.
7. **Series identity.** The build records BLS `CUUR0000SA0`, not merely "CPI", and never substitutes CPI-W.
8. **Vintage pinning.** The CSV SHA-256 from §2 is recorded. CPI-U is final when issued, so a changed hash for historical months indicates a BLS correction and requires a comparison report.

## 11. What is still missing

1. **CPI-W for Social Security COLA** (`CWUR0000SA0`), or the official SSA COLA history. `MARKET §5.2` forbids driving COLA from CPI-U. This is the next data gap once monthly stepping is real.
2. **Medical inflation** (`CUUR0000SAM`, `MARKET §5.3`) if the health-cost model is to be driven by data rather than an assumption.
3. **A named convention decision** — §5 shows the engine currently behaves as a December-to-December series. That must be stated in the engine package rather than inferred.
